facts.text: The muscles of my back, upper arms and thighs have become stiff.
Those same muscles have been wasting away.

facts.item: when the stiffness and wasting started
facts.text: The stiffness and wasting started about six years ago.

facts.item: course of the stiffness and wasting
facts.text: They have been getting steadily worse.
It isn't painful; I don't have any pain.
Walking is getting harder; I can only take short steps.

facts.item: difficulty getting up from lying down
facts.text: It's getting harder to get up from lying on my back.
It's getting harder to bend in any direction.
It's getting harder to lift my arms.
I can't move my thighs apart more than about 20 degrees.
I don't feel weak.
I haven't had any numbness or other change in feeling.
I don't get muscle spasms.
Six years ago I started injecting myself with pentazocine, 60 mg a day into my muscles.
I injected into my buttocks and upper arms.
I never injected my thighs, calves, abdomen, shoulder girdle or forearms.
I started the injections for abdominal pain, and I kept going because I became dependent.
I stopped the injections about six months after the stiffness began.
I injected promethazine together with it.
I was dependent on alcohol for 13 years.
I haven't had a drink for at least six years.
I don't have high blood pressure.
I don't have diabetes.
I'm right-handed.

findings.name: muscle examination
findings.result: Marked wasting and woody induration of the deltoids, biceps, glutei, quadriceps, and paraspinal muscles.

findings.name: range of motion
findings.result: Active range of motion markedly reduced: arm abduction to 45–50°, thigh abduction to 20°, elbow flexion to 15°, thigh flexion to 10°. Distal joint movements normal.

findings.name: motor strength
findings.result: Full power within the limited ranges.

findings.name: serum calcium and phosphate
findings.result: Calcium and phosphate within normal limits.

findings.name: X-rays of the lumbar spine, pelvis, thighs, knees, chest and shoulders
findings.result: Multiple soft-tissue calcifications with muscle hyperdensity.

gold.reasoning: 1. Ankylosing spondylitis was considered but excluded — “Ankylosing spondylitis was ruled out as there was no involvement of the joints.” 2. Stiff-man syndrome was considered but excluded — “Stiff-man syndrome presents with spasms and cramps, and usual presentation is after middle age. These features ruled out the possibility of this syndrome.” 3. Myositis ossificans was considered but deemed unlikely — “The possibility of myositis ossificans was unlikely, as the present case was of late onset and was characterized by the absence of skeletal abnormality.” 4. Hypoparathyroidism was considered but excluded — “Normal serum calcium and phosphate levels excluded hypoparathyroidism.” 5. Drug-induced calcific myofibrosis was favored — “Pentazocine-induced calcific myofibrosis was a strong possibility in view of the history of pentazocine abuse, calcified muscles and the clinical presentation.”

The radiograph report shows soft-tissue calcifications in the muscles (shares the stem of 'calcific'); a written report keeps its findings, and it does not name the diagnosis.
